summary.intent: Run the full E2E test suite against SDK extraction branch changes, diagnose failures, and restore CI coverage to a mergeable state.
summary.outcome: Fixed E2E import breakage from SDK extraction, migrated all 6 test suites from brittle Web3Auth test-login to wallet-based auth, fixed a race condition in the web app's auth flow, resolved rate-limiting flakiness, and added automatic key re-wrapping to the SDK — bringing the suite from 14 passing / 7 failing to 96 passing / 1 failing (pre-existing intermittent reload timing).

repo: The SDK extraction (this branch) moved initializeVault, encryptVaultKeys, decryptVaultKeys from @cipherbox/crypto to @cipherbox/core — E2E imports were not updated as part of the refactor.

E2E tests broken in CI since March 8 (PR #288) due to load-test.spec.ts being included in the default Playwright config and hanging for 10 min, causing the 15-min CI timeout to kill all tests. Root cause was not the someguy sidecar.
The someguy sidecar is only in the staging docker-compose and is not present in CI at all.

Web3Auth-based test login (loginViaTestEndpoint) requires Zustand state injection (reinjectTestAuthAfterReload) and is environment-dependent; wallet-based auth via @johanneskares/wallet-mock uses real SIWE flow and works in all environments without special config.
Conflict-detection tests hit the API rate limiter (10 req/s, 100/min) when bumpServerSequence is called rapidly across 3 consecutive serial tests — each call makes 2 API requests (resolve + publish).
Sharing test 7.3 was revealing a real app bug: files uploaded to a shared folder after sharing was established were not having their keys re-wrapped for share recipients.
The CipherBoxClient SDK was not performing automatic key re-wrapping on uploadFile/createFolder; this logic lived entirely in the web app layer.
sdk-core uploadFile did not return the plaintext file key, requiring a return type change to enable SDK-level re-wrapping.

code.finding: Race condition: setAccessToken() at line 259 sets isAuthenticated:true immediately, triggering Login.tsx redirect before initializeOrLoadVault() at line 265 completes — SDK client not initialized when files page loads. Fixed by adding setAuthenticated() action called only after vault+SDK init completes.
setAccessToken action was setting both accessToken and isAuthenticated:true. Split into setAccessToken (token only) and new setAuthenticated() action to decouple token storage from auth state.
Token refresh interceptor calls setAccessToken — this is a valid call site where the user is already authenticated, so setAuthenticated() call must also be added here after the token refresh.

loginViaWallet needed a waitForFunction check for vault keys in Zustand store to prevent SDK-not-initialized errors on subsequent file operations — vault init can still be in-flight when the /files page renders.

uploadFile and createFolder now call private reWrapNewItems() after publishing, which uses ShareCallbacks to find covering shares and re-wraps the item's encryption key for all recipients via ECIES. Emits share:reWrapFailed event on non-fatal errors.
Return type extended to include plaintext fileKey (Uint8Array) so the stateful CipherBoxClient can perform re-wrapping without re-deriving the key.
Manual re-wrapping logic removed after moving it into the SDK layer.
load-test.spec.ts excluded from default testMatch glob — it must be run explicitly, not as part of the standard CI suite.
Added 2s delay before bumpServerSequence calls to avoid rate limiting. Increased afterAll hook timeout to handle cleanup of multiple items after rate-limited test run.
Reload tests (3.8, 6.6.x) need vault-ready waitForFunction after page.reload() before asserting on folder contents — Core Kit session restoration is async and variable-latency from Sapphire Devnet.

workflow: When diagnosing CI test failures, check if a new test file was added without exclusion rules before assuming a code change is the root cause.

Wallet-mock based auth is strictly more reliable than test-login endpoint injection for E2E tests because it uses the real authentication flow and doesn't depend on environment-specific secrets or Zustand internals.
Serial Playwright test suites amplify flaky failures — one flaky test can skip 10+ downstream dependents. Fix the root cause rather than accepting high skip rates.
When a test reveals an actual app bug (like the re-wrapping failure), skipping it with a known-bug comment unblocks the suite but the correct resolution is to fix the app and remove the skip.

friction: TypeScript replace_all on 'TestAccount' also hit import type alias names (e.g. WalletTestAccount → WalletWalletTestAccount), requiring manual cleanup passes.
Background task output was delivered as stale notifications after the results had already been processed, creating noise.
The race condition fix required tracing through 4 separate call sites of setAccessToken across auth.store.ts, useAuth.ts, and client.ts to ensure none were missed.
Full-workflow 3.8 reload test remained intermittently flaky even after the vault-ready wait — Core Kit's Sapphire Devnet latency is non-deterministic and causes variable session restoration times.
1Password agent hiccup required a retry on one git commit.
Multiple rounds of re-running the full E2E suite were needed as fixes for one set of failures revealed new failures in different tests.
open_items: Full-workflow test 3.8 (reload subfolder navigation) remains intermittently flaky due to Core Kit Sapphire Devnet latency — timeout increases help but don't eliminate the flakiness. Consider mocking the IPNS resolution in reload tests or using a local devnet.
load-test.spec.ts has a pre-existing TypeScript error and is excluded from CI — needs its own dedicated run configuration and the type error fixed.
The reWrapNewItems SDK method should also be triggered on moveItem when a file is moved into a shared folder.
share:reWrapFailed event is emitted but the web app has no UI handler wired up to surface re-wrapping failures to users.
VITE_API_URL fallback in sdk-provider.ts uses window.location.origin + '/api' which would be wrong in production — should be validated at build time.
